Name: High-Complexity Medical Imaging Consolidated at Clinaltec
Subtitle: From fragmented technical workflows to a single cloud-native platform.
Executive Summary: Clinaltec, a Colombian institution specializing in high-complexity diagnostics, needed to modernize its medical imaging operation and consolidate visualization, storage, management, operational intelligence, and clinical integration of its studies on a single platform. The implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS enabled progress toward a more traceable, integrated, and scalable operation, with support for study upload and retrieval, user administration, productivity tracking, and initial adoption of artificial intelligence for medical report generation. This transformation has positioned Clinaltec to scale toward new sites and modalities.
Body:
The challenge

Operational consolidation in a highly complex technical environment

Clinaltec's operation is highly specialized across multiple modalities, including CT, MRI, mammography, angiography, nuclear medicine, SPECT, PET, and ultrasound. This presents key challenges:

  • Distributed operation: managing studies across different modalities required coordinating local servers, ensuring continuity in image migration, and advancing integration with internal systems to connect clinical information, patient location, medical history, and report delivery.
  • Specialized technical demands: operations in nuclear medicine and radiotherapy involve longer acquisition, reconstruction, and processing times, requiring deep technical understanding of the complete workflow.

The solution

An integral platform for advanced radiology

Clinaltec adopted Eden Diagnostic OS as a cloud-native platform, combining PACS, operational management, data intelligence, technical support, and adoption guidance.

The impact

Centralization and scalability

With Eden, Clinaltec advanced toward a more structured, traceable, and scalable medical imaging operation, moving from fragmented technical workflows to a platform that centralizes images, users, permissions, reports, metrics, and support:

  • Organized administration: centralized access, permissions, and support for all collaborators.
  • Operational visibility: productivity tracking, interpretation times, and study volume through Eden Intelligence.
  • Guided migration: continuity ensured during the migration of historical studies.
  • Ready to grow: infrastructure prepared to incorporate the second site in Girardot, new modalities such as ultrasound, and progressive adoption of artificial intelligence.

More than a technological installation, Clinaltec's case represents an operational transformation within a high-complexity institution: an implementation where Eden not only enabled software but accompanied the client in stabilizing infrastructure, driving clinical adoption, and building an operation better prepared to grow.

Name: Building a National Diagnostic Imaging Network at Dr. Simi
Subtitle: From distributed operations to a single cloud platform connecting 177 branches.
Executive Summary: Dr. Simi, one of Mexico's largest outpatient care networks, needed to scale access to medical imaging services nationwide without depending on infrastructure or specialists at every branch. Since 2022, the implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS has enabled centralized radiology interpretation, digital delivery of results to patients, and a scalable operation. Today, a single platform supports more than 177 branches and processes approximately 18,000 studies per month, sustaining the network's clinical continuity and capacity for growth.
Body:
The challenge

Scaling a nationally distributed imaging network

As Dr. Simi's imaging network began to expand, a complex operational challenge emerged: maintaining speed, diagnostic quality, and timely access to results across a network distributed at the national level. The organization faced key challenges:

  • Limited traditional model: operations depended on local infrastructure, manual processes, and specialist availability across multiple locations, which restricted growth capacity and generated friction for both operations and patients.
  • Patient experience: study delivery relied largely on in-person processes, while users demanded faster and simpler access to their images and reports.

The goal was not simply to store studies in the cloud: it was to build a national network capable of producing, interpreting, and delivering results from anywhere in the country.

The solution

A national platform for centralized cloud-based diagnostics

Dr. Simi adopted Eden Diagnostic OS as an integrated cloud platform, connecting branches, technicians, radiologists, and patients within a single digital ecosystem.

The impact

A national diagnostic network

With Eden, Dr. Simi shifted from managing studies in a distributed manner to operating a digitally connected national diagnostic network:

  • Centralization: 177 branches and 18,000 monthly studies operating on a single technology platform, leveraging available medical capacity by concentrating radiology reading in central locations rather than replicating it at every branch.
  • Best-in-class experience: patient experience transformed with immediate access to images and reports from any device.
  • Future scalability: consolidated infrastructure ready to incorporate new branches, imaging modalities, and artificial intelligence tools without redesigning the operation from scratch.

More than digitizing studies, the collaboration between Dr. Simi and Eden made it possible to build a national diagnostic platform capable of scaling access to medical imaging services while sustaining operational efficiency, clinical continuity, and a better experience for patients and healthcare professionals.

Name: Building a National Outpatient Diagnostic Operation at PROA
Subtitle: From a gradual migration to one of the largest operations running on Eden, with 379 branches and 140,000 monthly studies.
Executive Summary: PROA, one of Latin America's most important outpatient diagnostic operations, sought to regain flexibility and reduce the risk associated with depending on a single technology platform after years of experience with different PACS providers. The implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS, designed as a gradual and carefully controlled migration, evolved into one of the largest operations running on Eden. Today, PROA operates 379 branches and processes approximately 140,000 studies per month through the platform.
Body:
The challenge

Regaining flexibility and control over a critical imaging operation

PROA had a legitimate concern: avoiding once again becoming locked into a relationship of technological dependency. Previous experiences with different providers had generated a clear understanding of the risks of delegating a critical operation to inflexible platforms. The organization faced key challenges:

  • Technological dependency: unilateral changes in pricing, commercial terms, technical capabilities, or development priorities that could directly impact the organization's growth capacity.
  • Validation at real scale: the initial strategy did not consist of fully replacing the existing infrastructure, but rather validating in a controlled manner whether Eden could operate at the levels of stability, speed, and transparency that an organization of this scale required.

The solution

A progressive migration based on operational trust

Eden designed an implementation strategy based on progressive trust. Rather than requiring a complete migration from the start, the platform allowed PROA to incorporate operations gradually, validating results in real environments before making expansion decisions:

Controlled startMigration of a limited portion of the network
Coexistence with different PACS to reduce risks
Validation of stability, speed, and responsiveness in real environments
Staged expansionProgressive scaling of the platform's reach
Incorporation of hundreds of branches in less than three months
Adoption guided by observed results rather than by a fixed schedule
Joint accompanimentCoordinated work with PROA's clinical, operational, and technology teams
Assurance of operational continuity
Workflow integration and user adoption

Beyond the technology, one of the elements PROA valued most was the transparency of the relationship. The platform's openness, commercial flexibility, and capacity for adaptation generated a model of collaboration different from what the organization had traditionally experienced with other PACS providers.

The impact

From a partial migration to a consolidated national operation

What was initially proposed as a partial implementation ultimately evolved into a continuous expansion of the operation. As PROA verified the results obtained, it gradually increased the percentage of studies and branches operated by Eden until making it one of its principal medical imaging environments:

  • Consolidated scale: 379 branches and approximately 140,000 monthly studies operating on a single platform.
  • Recovered control: a critical operation sustained without sacrificing growth speed, technological stability, or negotiating capacity.
  • Relationship based on transparency: openness of the platform, commercial flexibility, and capacity for adaptation that generated a model of collaboration distinct from the traditional one.
  • Strategic alliance: transformation of an originally defensive decision (avoiding technological dependency) into a long-term alliance for the organization's growth.

For PROA, the migration did not represent merely a change of PACS. It represented the construction of a technological relationship based on transparency, flexibility, and mutual trust.

Name: Integrating Specialized Artificial Intelligence at Pulso Salud
Subtitle: An integrated platform with AI applied to chest studies for occupational medicine at scale.
Executive Summary: Pulso Salud, an organization specialized in occupational medicine for high-demand sectors such as mining, industry, and energy, needed a platform capable of supporting high volumes of diagnostic studies, integrating with its internal systems, and leveraging new technologies to optimize its processes. The implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS made it possible to build an integrated digital operation in which medical images, clinical systems, and artificial intelligence tools work in a coordinated way. Today, Pulso Salud operates 19 branches and processes between 16,000 and 17,000 studies per month on the platform.
Body:
The challenge

Sustaining high volumes of occupational studies without operational friction

Pulso Salud primarily serves workers in industries with high operational demands, where imaging studies are part of critical processes related to workplace safety, medical fitness, and regulatory compliance. This brings challenges such as:

  • Sustained volume with fast turnaround: the operation required handling high volumes of studies consistently, maintaining fast response times and avoiding friction between the various systems involved in the workflow.
  • High concentration of chest studies: a significant portion of the operation is concentrated in chest studies, a fundamental modality for occupational surveillance programs and follow-up of workers exposed to various risk factors. The challenge was to maintain productivity and diagnostic quality without increasing the operational burden on medical teams.

The solution

An integrated platform with specialized AI

Eden implemented a comprehensive cloud platform designed to integrate with Pulso Salud's existing clinical operation, combining image management, technical connectivity, and artificial intelligence applied to the highest-volume modality:

Technical integrationEden PACS & Eden Management
Development of integrations with the systems and protocols used by the organization
Automatic information flow between the tools involved in patient care
Reduction of manual processes and improved traceability of information
Specialized Artificial IntelligenceEden AI Thorax
Support for the review and prioritization of findings in chest studies
A more agile and consistent operation in high-volume scenarios
Support for medical teams in the modality of highest concentration

The impact

An advanced operation for occupational medicine at scale

With Eden, Pulso Salud consolidated a connected medical imaging operation, where studies are managed, stored, and accessed centrally while clinical information flows in an integrated way across the organization's systems:

  • Volume processed: between 16,000 and 17,000 monthly studies on the platform, distributed across a network of 19 branches.
  • Clinical integration: automatic flow of information between internal systems and the imaging platform, reducing manual processes and operational friction.
  • AI applied to volume: incorporation of artificial intelligence for chest studies, strengthening the capacity to operate large volumes of occupational exams consistently.
  • Ready to grow: infrastructure prepared to scale without proportionally increasing administrative or technical complexity.

More than a technological implementation, the project enabled Pulso Salud to build a platform capable of supporting the growth of an organization specialized in occupational medicine, where speed, integration, and scalability are fundamental elements for operational success.

Name: Modernizing Imaging Operations at Hospital Metropolitano
Subtitle: A technological layer integrated with internal systems, without replacing what already works.
Executive Summary: Hospital Metropolitano, one of Costa Rica's leading private hospital networks, had administrative, clinical, and operational processes built around internally developed systems. Any modernization project had to respect the continuity of those workflows. The implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS served as a medical imaging technology layer integrated with the existing infrastructure, making it possible to modernize the radiology operation without forcing the hospital to modify its core systems. Today, Hospital Metropolitano processes approximately 12,000 studies per month on the platform.
Body:
The challenge

Modernizing the radiology operation without disrupting institutional processes

Like many healthcare organizations with years of technological evolution, Hospital Metropolitano had developed internal systems and processes that supported critical business activities. The organization faced key challenges:

  • Operational continuity: the implementation of a new medical imaging platform could not affect the existing clinical, administrative, and financial operation.
  • Adaptation to the hospital's technological reality: the risk in any project of this kind lies in causing disruptions, duplicating operational work, or forcing users to modify processes they already master. The hospital needed a solution capable of adapting to its technological reality.

The solution

A medical imaging platform as an interoperability layer

Eden implemented a cloud platform designed to integrate with Hospital Metropolitano's existing systems. Rather than replacing processes, the platform was designed to extend and complement them:

Integration with internal systemsDevelopment of specific integrations to connect the radiology operation with existing administrative and clinical tools
Preservation of the workflows that physicians, technicians, administrative staff, and operational teams already mastered
Reduced impact of change for end users
Advanced capabilities over the existing operationEden PACS
Storage, visualization, distribution, and management of medical studies
Incorporation of modern diagnostic capabilities without replacing critical systems
Operational continuity throughout the implementation

The impact

High-specialty technology without replacing critical systems

With Eden, Hospital Metropolitano modernized its medical imaging operation without the need to replace critical systems or redesign institutional processes:

  • Volume processed: approximately 12,000 studies per month on the platform.
  • Institutional continuity: integration with internally developed tools, preserving existing administrative, clinical, and operational processes.
  • Ecosystem extension: a platform that functions as a natural extension of the hospital's infrastructure, connecting medical images, users, and systems within a single digital ecosystem.

More than a PACS implementation, the project represented an interoperability exercise at scale, demonstrating that technological innovation in healthcare can be built while respecting the processes that already generate value within an organization.

Name: Unifying Eight Medical Imaging Departments at Grupo Dalinde San Ángel Inn
Subtitle: From eight hospitals with distinct technological histories to a group-wide radiology operation on a single platform.
Executive Summary: Grupo Dalinde San Ángel Inn, a hospital network comprising eight hospitals that had historically operated with different providers, systems, and levels of technological maturity, needed to convert that fragmentation into an integrated clinical operation. The implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS supported the complete migration of all eight sites, integrating imaging workflows from diverse environments, including systems such as Fuji Synapse and Carestream by Philips, and enabling a common platform for visualization, interpretation, storage, interoperability, and study management. Today, DSAI processes approximately 15,000 studies per month on the platform.
Body:
The challenge

Building a common operational standard across a fragmented hospital network

DSAI's main challenge was not simply changing PACS, but integrating a hospital network built from independent operations. Each hospital had its own technological history, its own processes, and its own way of operating medical imaging. The organization faced key challenges:

  • Operational heterogeneity: differences in protocols, administrative systems, workflows, data capture, study retrieval, and interpretation tools across the eight sites.
  • Isolation between hospitals: physicians had less visibility into studies performed at other sites, operational teams had to adapt to different processes depending on the hospital, and the institution lost the ability to manage medical imaging as a single group operation.

The solution

A phased migration toward a common platform across the entire network

Eden implemented a migration and integration strategy designed to respect the group's heterogeneous reality and build a common operation. The project was structured in two phases:

Pilot testInitial validation at three hospitals: HSAI Sur, HSAI Universidad, and Centro Médico Dalinde
Verification of technical viability and performance of advanced diagnostic tools
Confirmation of interoperability between hospitals
Full network migrationStandardization of imaging workflows across the eight sites
User configuration, training, and integration with administrative systems
Connection with worklists and migration of historical studies
Connection of orders from internal systems to medical modalities
Enabled retrieval of historical studies and access to images and reports from any hospital in the group

The impact

From eight independent hospitals to a group radiology operation

With Eden, DSAI moved from a fragmented hospital operation to a more integrated, standardized, and collaborative medical imaging network:

  • Consolidated operation: eight sites and approximately 15,000 monthly studies on a single platform, regardless of each hospital's prior systems.
  • Cross-site interoperability: credentialed physicians can consult, access, and report studies according to permissions and roles, supporting collaboration between hospitals and the leverage of shared medical resources.
  • Digital experience for patients and referring physicians: more efficient access to images and results, with reduced dependence on physical printouts.
  • Group-level technology foundation: centralization that makes it possible to optimize costs, improve traceability, and build a homogeneous radiology operation on a single technology layer.

More than a PACS migration, the DSAI case represents a network transformation: the conversion of eight hospitals with distinct technological histories into a common medical imaging operation, integrated on a single platform.

Name: Building a Centralized Architecture for Hospitals and Teleradiology at Dasa and Lumiax
Subtitle: A single platform supporting enterprise hospital operations and distributed teleradiology, with more than 55,000 monthly studies.
Executive Summary: Dasa, the largest diagnostic medicine group in Brazil and one of the largest in Latin America, operates dozens of regional brands and units distributed across multiple states. Its teleradiology unit, Lumiax, brings together a network of more than one hundred independent clients with their own systems, modalities, and protocols. The collaboration with Eden had two strategic components: the implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS in the São Marcos operations and the group's outsourced processes, with eleven units distributed across three Brazilian states, and the technological transformation of Lumiax, where Eden became the exclusive provider of the platform supporting its diagnostic operation. Today, the combined operation processes approximately 55,000 studies per month: nearly 15,000 from Dasa's direct operations and more than 40,000 from the Lumiax teleradiology network.
Body:
The challenge

Simultaneously supporting a hospital operation and a distributed teleradiology network

Most hospital implementation projects involve deploying a platform within one organization. Dasa and Lumiax presented an entirely different challenge:

  • Operational diversity at Lumiax: the network comprised dozens of independent clients, each with different systems, processes, modalities, and protocols, as well as independent work teams with their own operational needs. There was no single workflow, but dozens of workflows coexisting at the same time.
  • Diagnostic continuity during migration: Lumiax needed to maintain continuity for all its clients while migrating the operation, without the particularities of each new unit (specific configurations, technical validations, differentiated training, operational support) interrupting service.
  • A common architecture for two distinct realities: the operation included both Dasa's direct hospitals and the Lumiax distributed teleradiology network, requiring a single platform capable of supporting two care models.

The solution

A scalable rollout with continuous product evolution

Eden designed a deployment strategy capable of absorbing Lumiax's operational diversity without losing standardization, while supporting the rollout across Dasa's direct operations. The project was structured around three components:

Simultaneous go-live65 independent units activated in a single implementation milestone
Subsequent growth surpassing 100 active units
Support for different modalities, capture processes, and local teams at each unit
Rollout across Dasa's direct operationsImplementation across the São Marcos brands and outsourced processes
Eleven units distributed across three Brazilian states
Shared architecture with the Lumiax teleradiology operation
Continuous product evolution36 specific improvements and features developed in approximately four months
Adjustments to workflows, process automation, operational management tools, enhancements for radiologists, integrations, and performance optimizations
Eden's continuous development model, which incorporates more than 1,500 improvements and features each year

The impact

A unified imaging services platform across an entire region

Dasa and Lumiax today represent one of the largest ecosystems operating on Eden Diagnostic OS in Brazil.

  • Consolidated volume: more than 55,000 monthly studies, combining 15,000 from Dasa's direct operations and more than 40,000 from the Lumiax teleradiology network.
  • Dual model: a single platform sustains a large-scale enterprise hospital network and a distributed teleradiology operation with more than one hundred independent centers.
  • Full standardization: centralization of studies, homogeneous diagnostic processes, operational traceability, and a consistent experience for radiologists and clinical teams, regardless of the study's origin.
  • Internal turning point: the scale of the rollout required Eden to redesign processes, professionalize implementation mechanisms, and strengthen operational capabilities that later became standards for other projects at the company.

What began as a complex implementation became proof that Eden operates successfully in some of the most demanding and scalable environments of the Latin American imaging market.

Name: Creating a National Imaging Network for the Government of El Salvador
Subtitle: More than 60 institutions connected in a single technological architecture for imaging and teleradiology.
Executive Summary: The Government of El Salvador launched a strategy to modernize and standardize imaging and teleradiology workflows at the national level, creating a network capable of connecting hospitals, care centers, specialists, and clinical systems under a single technological architecture. Eden was selected as the technology partner through the implementation of Eden Diagnostic OS, interoperability services, and operational coordination tools. By the end of the deployment, the network includes more than 60 institutions distributed across the country, comprising one of the most ambitious interoperability and imaging projects in the region.
Body:
The challenge

Unifying a national health system

National health systems often face a common challenge: the coexistence of multiple institutions, systems, processes, and levels of technological maturity. The Government of El Salvador's modernization strategy faced key challenges:

  • Institutional fragmentation: each hospital or care center operated with different tools, different workflows, and variable capabilities to manage medical imaging studies, hindering collaboration between institutions and limiting visibility of clinical information.
  • Unequal access to specialized services: fragmentation created barriers to scaling services such as teleradiology, restricting access to specialized diagnostic interpretation across different regions of the country.
  • Continuity during transformation: the solution had to integrate with existing systems, respect established institutional processes, and maintain operational continuity throughout the transformation.

The solution

A national imaging platform with institutional interoperability

Eden implemented a platform designed to connect institutions, clinical systems, and medical teams within a single operational network. The deployment was structured around three components:

Institutional interoperabilityA specialized integration layer to coordinate orders, studies, operational statuses, and diagnostic results across multiple systems
Synchronization of clinical information among participating institutions
Traceability across the entire study lifecycle
Teleradiology networkDistribution of diagnostic workload across specialists
Optimized use of medical resources
Extended radiology interpretation coverage for institutions across different regions
Adaptation to the Salvadoran health systemJoint work with clinical, operational, and technology teams
Prioritization of interoperability, scalability, and service continuity
Respect for established institutional processes

The impact

A national infrastructure to coordinate imaging across institutions

With Eden, the Government of El Salvador advanced toward a national imaging network that is more connected, standardized, and ready to grow:

  • National coverage: more than 60 healthcare institutions incorporated into a single operational network.
  • Collaboration between institutions: infrastructure that facilitates the exchange of clinical information and improves traceability of orders and studies across care centers.
  • Expanded access to specialists: teleradiology processes that allow institutions with different capabilities to integrate within a single care network.

Beyond the implementation of a technology platform, the project represents a step toward building a national digital health ecosystem, where hospitals, care centers, and healthcare professionals can share information more efficiently, in a coordinated and secure way, for the benefit of patients across the country.
